## What I did

I agree with the finding. Reusing `normalizeHouseholdValue` for city comparison tied a household-named helper to an unrelated concern, making the `countOwnersInCity` call site misleading and coupling city-matching semantics to future household changes.

I extracted a domain-neutral helper **`normalizeForComparison`** (same trim/collapse-whitespace/lowercase logic) and updated its Javadoc to describe it as general equality canonicalization shared by both the household and per-city rules. All ten call sites — the household methods (`isHouseholdInUse`, `inHousehold`, `assignHousehold`, `generateHouseholdId`) and the new `countOwnersInCity` — now reference the neutral name. Behaviour is unchanged (identical normalization logic), so the acceptance test still passes.
